# Mandatory receipts can turn committed legacy writes into reported failures
P1 structural compatibility pattern: an independently shipped consumer begins requiring a new application receipt unconditionally, while the supported legacy provider commits the write and returns only its existing success acknowledgement. The consumer then reports failure after persistence, including on retries; a disabled feature flag offers no protection when the shared save path enforces receipts. Updating a success mock to emit the new field masks this mixed-version failure. Verify with actual supported provider source and assert both persisted state and caller-visible success; retain a legacy path until receipt capability is established, while rejecting explicit negative receipts. Encountered during isolated review of enhanced-settings task 1: staged client.py lines 2 and 5–6, provider/settings.py at eval-release (22140737b2bc5792b535f3f8ce16f7fa162101db). Parent reproduced previous-client success versus candidate exception after the same provider mutation. No live deployment claim.
